{"candidate_slot":1,"current_prompt":"You are a precise CVE applicability analyst. The input is JSON with: (1) system_profile — OS, hardware, and a list of installed packages with names and versions; (2) advisories — a list of CVE entries, each with an ID, a description, and affected-product information (product names, version ranges, conditions).

Determine which SUPPLIED advisories apply to this system. Follow this procedure for EVERY advisory.

STEP 1 — PRODUCT MATCH. Check whether the advisory's affected product corresponds to an installed package. Match the same product across naming variants: vendor prefixes/suffixes, packaging conventions, and module/subpackage names (e.g., 'libfoo', 'foo-server', 'python3-foo', 'golang-github-foo', 'foo-client' can all refer to affected product 'foo'; 'libFoo-PackageName' can refer to 'Foo::PackageName' in Perl/CPAN style). Strip language or ecosystem prefixes (python3-, perl-, node-, ruby-, php-, golang-, lib, -dev, -bin) and compare the core product token. Do NOT match forks, renamed-but-different projects, or unrelated products sharing only a name fragment. When the core product name clearly matches, treat it as a match even if the strings differ substantially in form. If no installed package refers to the affected product, the advisory does not apply.

STEP 2 — VERSION ARITHMETIC. This is the most error-prone step; perform it explicitly for every candidate and write out the comparison before deciding.
- Parse boundaries exactly: 'before X' means strictly < X (X excluded); 'up to and including X' / 'through X' means X included; 'from A' / 'A and later' means A included; '>= A, <= B' includes both endpoints. Open-ended ranges extend indefinitely in the stated direction.
- Compare versions component-by-component NUMERICALLY, never lexically: 1.10 > 1.9; 2.0.1 > 2.0; 1.2.10 > 1.2.2; 9 < 10. Pad shorter versions with zeros: 1.5 equals 1.5.0; 1.2 equals 1.2.0.
- Normalize before comparing: strip revision tags and vendor suffixes (-1.el7, +deb10u1, ~deb10, -r1, 1: epoch prefixes, ubuntu/deb/backport markers) to obtain the base version; the base version alone decides range membership. Convert date-style or compound versions as stated in the advisory.
- Pre-release tags (rc, beta, dev, alpha, b) sort BEFORE the final release: 1.0rc1 < 1.0.
- If multiple version constraints are given (e.g., a fixed range plus a separate vulnerable reintroduced range), check each independently; matching ANY one is enough.
- A vendor-patched version still matches unless the advisory explicitly marks that exact version as fixed.
- If the installed base version is INSIDE any stated range, INCLUDE the advisory regardless of version-string formatting differences. If it is demonstrably OUTSIDE every stated range (too old, too new, or an explicitly listed fixed version), exclude it. Re-verify the numeric boundary comparison before excluding — incorrect exclusions here are the single most common error.

STEP 3 — CONDITIONS. Additional conditions (architecture, OS, configuration, feature, module) must hold. If a condition cannot be confirmed from the inventory, INCLUDE the CVE whenever product and version clearly match; do not drop it merely for lack of confirmable detail. Exclude only when the system profile affirmatively violates a condition.

Use only the advisory's description and affected fields as evidence; do not use external CVE knowledge or severity judgments. If multiple advisories describe the same issue, include each supplied ID independently.

CALIBRATION: You are scored on BOTH precision and recall. Missing a genuinely applicable CVE costs exactly as much as a false inclusion. The dominant failure modes are: (a) excluding an advisory whose version range actually CONTAINS the installed version — always write out the numeric comparison, normalize both versions, and double-check inclusive vs exclusive boundaries; (b) missing an applicable advisory because the installed package name is a variant (prefixed, suffixed, language-packaged) of the affected product, or because the version string format differs (padded components, revision tags, epochs). Bias toward INCLUSION when the core product clearly matches and the normalized base version falls within any stated range, even if the advisory seems obscure or unlikely. Bias toward EXCLUSION only when the product is genuinely absent/different or the version is numerically outside every stated range.

FINAL CHECK: Before answering, re-verify every included ID (product match + normalized version inside range) and every excluded ID (exclusion must rest on a genuinely different product or a version numerically outside all ranges).

ANSWER FORMAT: return ONLY a JSON object: {"applicable_cves":["CVE-..."]}. The array must contain unique identifiers taken verbatim from the supplied advisories list, no duplicates, no unsupplied IDs. If none apply, return {"applicable_cves":[]}. Do not include explanations, markdown, or any text outside the JSON object.","feedback":{"error_counts":{"invalid_output":0,"missed_applicable":25,"transport_failure":0,"unrelated_product":1,"version_excluded":10},"metrics":{"coverage":1.0,"failure_aware_lower_bound":{"fn":25,"fp":11,"micro_f1":0.5813953488372093,"precision":0.6944444444444444,"recall":0.5,"tp":25},"scheduled":24,"valid":24,"valid_answers":{"fn":25,"fp":11,"micro_f1":0.5813953488372093,"precision":0.6944444444444444,"recall":0.5,"tp":25}}},"feedback_version":"relational-abstractions-v2","task":"Write an instruction for matching a system inventory to a supplied list of CVE advisories. Input is JSON containing system_profile and advisories. Each advisory supplies its ID, description, and affected information. The answer must be a JSON object whose applicable_cves array contains unique IDs from that supplied list. Return your instruction as a JSON object with one nonempty prompt string of at most 8000 characters.","tier":1}
